# package rsession

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/rsession"
```

Package rsession carries GOOSE and Sampled Values over UDP/IP: R-GOOSE and R-SV, with the session protocol of IEC TR 61850-90-5 and its per-SPDU authentication (HMAC-SHA256).

#### Using it {#hdr-Using_it}

A [Transport](#type-transport) implements the layer-2 transport interface of packages goose and sv, so their publishers and subscribers run over UDP unchanged:

	keys, _ := rsession.NewKeyRing(rsession.Key{ID: 1, Material: secret, MAC: rsession.MACHMACSHA256_128})
	t, _ := rsession.Open(rsession.Config{
		SI:         rsession.SIGOOSE,
		RemoteAddr: netip.MustParseAddrPort("239.192.0.1:102"),
		Keys:       keys,
	})
	pub, _ := goose.NewPublisher(t, goose.PublisherConfig{...})

and on the receiving side

	t, _ := rsession.Open(rsession.Config{
		SI:     rsession.SIGOOSE,
		Groups: []netip.Addr{netip.MustParseAddr("239.192.0.1")},
		Keys:   keys,
	})
	sub, _ := goose.NewSubscriber(t, goose.SubscriberConfig{})

The publisher's Ethernet addresses and VLAN tag are not sent; frames a receiving Transport returns carry [Config.FrameDst](#func-config-framedst) and [SourceMAC](#func-sourcemac) of the sender instead.

#### Security {#hdr-Security}

Secured is the default: [Open](#func-open) refuses a configuration without a [KeyProvider](#type-keyprovider) unless [Config.Insecure](#func-config-insecure) is set, and a receiver refuses unsecured SPDUs unless it is set. A receiver also refuses SPDUs under keys it does not hold, SPDUs whose signature does not verify, and replays: per sender and key, an SPDU number accepted before or older than the ReplayWindow. Refusals are counted ([Transport.Stats](#func-transport-stats)) and reported to [Config.OnReject](#func-config-onreject).

Keys come from a [KeyProvider](#type-keyprovider): the current key secures what is sent, every key it holds is accepted on receipt. [KeyRing](#type-keyring) is a static provider; key distribution (IEC 62351-9 GDOI) is outside this package.

Only HMAC-SHA256 (80, 128 and 256 bits) is implemented: AES-GMAC and encryption are refused as ErrUnsupported. The layer-2 IEC 62351-6 extension of GOOSE and SV frames is not implemented. See docs/adr/0001-routable-goose-sv.md for the wire layout, the references it follows and the scope.

#### Codec {#hdr-Codec}

[Encode](#func-encode), [Decode](#func-decode) and [Verify](#func-verify) work on single SPDUs without a socket, for captures and tests.

## Constants

```go
const DefaultMaxSenders = 1024
```

DefaultMaxSenders bounds the replay state a [Transport](#type-transport) keeps.

```go
const DefaultPort = 102
```

DefaultPort is the UDP port of R-GOOSE and R-SV.

```go
const DefaultQueue = 1024
```

DefaultQueue is the receive queue length of a [Transport](#type-transport).

```go
const MaxSPDUSize = 65507
```

MaxSPDUSize is the largest SPDU encoded or decoded: the largest UDP payload over IPv4.

```go
const MinKeySize = 16
```

MinKeySize is the minimum key material length accepted, in octets.

```go
const ReplayWindow = 64
```

ReplayWindow is the number of SPDU numbers below the highest accepted one that may still arrive once each (reordering on the network).

## Variables

```go
var (
	// ErrMalformed indicates a datagram that is not a well-formed SPDU:
	// a wrong transport header, a length that runs past the datagram,
	// a truncated field or trailing octets.
	ErrMalformed = errors.New("rsession: malformed SPDU")

	// ErrUnsupported indicates a well-formed SPDU that uses something
	// this package does not implement: a protocol version other than 1
	// or 2, encryption, or a MAC algorithm other than HMAC-SHA256.
	ErrUnsupported = errors.New("rsession: unsupported")

	// ErrUnsecured indicates an SPDU without a key ID and signature,
	// refused unless unsecured SPDUs are allowed.
	ErrUnsecured = errors.New("rsession: unsecured SPDU")

	// ErrUnknownKey indicates an SPDU secured with a key ID that the
	// key provider does not hold.
	ErrUnknownKey = errors.New("rsession: unknown key")

	// ErrAuthentication indicates a secured SPDU whose signature is
	// missing, has the wrong length or algorithm, or does not verify.
	ErrAuthentication = errors.New("rsession: authentication failed")

	// ErrReplay indicates an SPDU whose number was already accepted
	// from the same sender under the same key, or is older than the
	// replay window.
	ErrReplay = errors.New("rsession: replayed SPDU")

	// ErrNoKey indicates that the key provider has no current key to
	// secure an SPDU with.
	ErrNoKey = errors.New("rsession: no current key")

	// ErrInvalidKey indicates a key that cannot be used: ID 0, no or
	// too short key material, or an unsupported MAC algorithm.
	ErrInvalidKey = errors.New("rsession: invalid key")

	// ErrInvalidFrame indicates a frame passed to [Transport.Send] that
	// is not a layer-2 GOOSE or SV frame of the transport's kind.
	ErrInvalidFrame = errors.New("rsession: invalid frame")

	// ErrLimitExceeded indicates an SPDU that would exceed
	// [MaxSPDUSize] or an APDU longer than the 16-bit APDU length.
	ErrLimitExceeded = errors.New("rsession: limit exceeded")

	// ErrInvalidConfig indicates an invalid transport configuration. It
	// is the l2 value, shared with packages goose and sv.
	ErrInvalidConfig = l2.ErrInvalidConfig

	// ErrClosed indicates an operation on a closed transport. It is the
	// l2 value, shared with packages goose and sv.
	ErrClosed = l2.ErrClosed

	// ErrUnsupportedPlatform indicates that multicast group membership
	// or multicast socket options are not available on this platform.
	// It is the l2 value.
	ErrUnsupportedPlatform = l2.ErrUnsupportedPlatform
)
```

Sentinel errors returned by the rsession package. Use [errors.Is](https://pkg.go.dev/errors#Is) to test against them. Decoder failures are [\*DecodeError](#type-decodeerror) values that unwrap to ErrMalformed or ErrUnsupported; verification failures wrap ErrUnsecured, ErrUnknownKey, ErrAuthentication or ErrReplay.

## Functions

### func AppendSPDU

```go
func AppendSPDU(dst []byte, s *SPDU, key *Key) ([]byte, error)
```

AppendSPDU appends the wire encoding of s, secured with key (nil for unsecured), to dst. The layout, in network byte order:

	01 40                          connectionless transport header
	SI LI                          session identifier, session header length
	80 0A length(4) number(4) version(2)
	v1: timeOfCurrentKey(4) timeToNextKey(2) encryption(1) mac(1) keyID(4)
	v2: timeOfCurrentKey(4) timeToNextKey(2) keyID(4) ivLength(1) iv
	payloadLength(4)
	{ type(1) simulation(1) APPID(2) APDULength(2) APDU }...
	85 len MAC                     when secured

The session header length counts the octets after it to the end of the security information; the SPDU length counts the octets after it to the end of the SPDU. The MAC covers everything before its tag.

### func Encode

```go
func Encode(s *SPDU, key *Key) ([]byte, error)
```

Encode returns the wire encoding of s, secured with key; key nil sends it unsecured (key ID 0, no signature).

### func SourceMAC

```go
func SourceMAC(addr netip.Addr) l2.MAC
```

SourceMAC returns the source address of the frames [Transport.Recv](#func-transport-recv) rebuilds from SPDUs sent by addr, so that subscribers keep the streams of different senders apart and can filter on them. It is a locally administered unicast address: 02-00 followed by the four octets of an IPv4 address, or 02 followed by the first five octets of the SHA-256 of an IPv6 address.

### func Verify

```go
func Verify(b []byte, opts VerifyOptions) (*SPDU, *Key, error)
```

Verify decodes b and checks its signature. It returns the SPDU and the key that verified it (nil for an accepted unsecured SPDU).

An SPDU is unsecured when its key ID is 0 (and, in version 1, its MAC algorithm is none) and it has no signature; it is refused with ErrUnsecured unless opts.AllowUnsecured. A secured SPDU is refused with ErrUnknownKey when the provider does not hold its key, with ErrUnsupported when it is encrypted or uses a MAC algorithm other than HMAC-SHA256, and with ErrAuthentication when the signature is missing, its length or algorithm does not match the key, or it does not verify. Replay is checked by [Transport](#type-transport), not here.

## Types

### type Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// SI selects what the transport carries: [SIGOOSE] (layer-2 frames
	// of EtherType 0x88B8) or [SISV] (0x88BA). Required.
	SI SessionID

	// LocalAddr is the address to bind. The zero value binds the
	// wildcard address, on [DefaultPort] when Groups is set and on an
	// ephemeral port otherwise (enough for a sender). Binding port 102
	// needs privileges on most systems.
	LocalAddr netip.AddrPort

	// RemoteAddr is where [Transport.Send] sends: a unicast address or a
	// multicast group. The zero value makes the transport receive-only.
	// A zero port means [DefaultPort].
	RemoteAddr netip.AddrPort

	// Groups are multicast groups to join for receiving.
	Groups []netip.Addr

	// Interface names the network interface for multicast: the groups
	// are joined on it and multicast is sent from it. Empty lets the
	// system choose.
	Interface string

	// MulticastTTL is the IPv4 TTL or IPv6 hop limit of multicast sent;
	// 0 keeps the system default (1, which does not cross a router).
	MulticastTTL int

	// Keys secures what is sent and verifies what is received. Nil
	// requires Insecure.
	Keys KeyProvider

	// Insecure is the explicit opt-in to unsecured SPDUs: with Keys nil
	// they are sent unsecured, and in any case unsecured SPDUs are
	// accepted on receipt. Secured SPDUs are still verified.
	Insecure bool

	// Version is the session protocol version sent, 1 or 2; 0 means 2.
	// Both are received.
	Version uint16

	// InitialSPDUNumber is the number of the first SPDU sent. A
	// publisher that restarts can continue from a persisted
	// [Transport.NextSPDUNumber] so that receivers do not take its
	// SPDUs for replays.
	InitialSPDUNumber uint32

	// ReplayResetAfter, when positive, lets a sender restart its SPDU
	// numbering: an SPDU older than the replay window is accepted if
	// nothing was accepted from that sender and key for this long.
	// Zero refuses it until the key changes.
	ReplayResetAfter time.Duration

	// MaxSenders bounds the replay state; zero means
	// [DefaultMaxSenders]. The sender heard from least recently is
	// forgotten first.
	MaxSenders int

	// Queue is the receive queue length; zero means [DefaultQueue].
	// Frames that do not fit are dropped and counted.
	Queue int

	// FrameDst is the destination address of the frames [Transport.Recv]
	// returns; zero means [l2.Broadcast]. The source address is
	// [SourceMAC] of the sender.
	FrameDst l2.MAC

	// HardwareAddr is returned by [Transport.HardwareAddr], the default
	// source address of a publisher. It is not sent.
	HardwareAddr l2.MAC

	// OnReject, when non-nil, is called with every refused datagram's
	// sender and the reason, for a security event log. It runs on the
	// receive goroutine and must not block.
	OnReject func(from netip.AddrPort, err error)

	// Logger receives transport diagnostics. Nil disables logging.
	Logger *slog.Logger

	// Now returns the current time; nil uses [time.Now]. For tests.
	Now func() time.Time
}
```

Config configures a [Transport](#type-transport).

### type EncryptionAlgorithm

```go
type EncryptionAlgorithm uint8
```

EncryptionAlgorithm identifies the encryption algorithm octet of a protocol version 1 SPDU. Encryption is not implemented: an SPDU with a value other than EncryptionNone is refused with ErrUnsupported.

```go
const (
	EncryptionNone   EncryptionAlgorithm = 0
	EncryptionAES128 EncryptionAlgorithm = 1 // AES-128-GCM, not implemented
	EncryptionAES256 EncryptionAlgorithm = 2 // AES-256-GCM, not implemented
)
```

Encryption algorithms (IEC TR 61850-90-5 code points).

### type Key

```go
type Key struct {
	// ID identifies the key in the SPDU header. 0 is reserved for
	// unsecured SPDUs.
	ID uint32

	// Material is the secret, at least [MinKeySize] octets.
	Material []byte

	// MAC is the signature algorithm used with this key. In protocol
	// version 2 the algorithm is a property of the key ID and not
	// carried on the wire.
	MAC MACAlgorithm

	// TimeOfCurrentKey and TimeToNextKey are sent verbatim in the
	// security information of every SPDU secured with this key. Their
	// meaning (when the key became current, how long until the next
	// one) belongs to the key management in use.
	TimeOfCurrentKey uint32
	TimeToNextKey    int16
}
```

Key is a symmetric key that secures SPDUs.

### type KeyProvider

```go
type KeyProvider interface {
	// CurrentKey returns the key that secures the next SPDU sent, or
	// an error wrapping [ErrNoKey].
	CurrentKey() (*Key, error)

	// LookupKey returns the key with the given ID, used to verify a
	// received SPDU, and whether it is known.
	LookupKey(id uint32) (*Key, bool)
}
```

KeyProvider supplies the keys of a [Transport](#type-transport). Implementations must be safe for concurrent use; they are called for every SPDU sent and received, so they should not block.

An application with its own key distribution (for example IEC 62351-9 GDOI) implements KeyProvider over it; [KeyRing](#type-keyring) is a static provider.

### type KeyRing

```go
type KeyRing struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

KeyRing is a static, concurrency-safe [KeyProvider](#type-keyprovider). It holds any number of keys, all accepted on receipt, and one current key used to send. A key change without loss is: Add the new key at every receiver, SetCurrent at the sender, then Remove the old key.

#### func NewKeyRing

```go
func NewKeyRing(keys ...Key) (*KeyRing, error)
```

NewKeyRing returns a key ring holding keys; the first one is current. It fails with ErrInvalidKey for an invalid or duplicate key.

#### func (KeyRing) Add

```go
func (r *KeyRing) Add(k Key) error
```

Add adds a copy of k. It fails with ErrInvalidKey if k is invalid or its ID is already present.

#### func (KeyRing) CurrentKey

```go
func (r *KeyRing) CurrentKey() (*Key, error)
```

CurrentKey implements [KeyProvider](#type-keyprovider).

#### func (KeyRing) LookupKey

```go
func (r *KeyRing) LookupKey(id uint32) (*Key, bool)
```

LookupKey implements [KeyProvider](#type-keyprovider).

#### func (KeyRing) Remove

```go
func (r *KeyRing) Remove(id uint32)
```

Remove removes the key with the given ID. Removing the current key leaves the ring without one until [KeyRing.SetCurrent](#func-keyring-setcurrent).

#### func (KeyRing) SetCurrent

```go
func (r *KeyRing) SetCurrent(id uint32) error
```

SetCurrent makes the key with the given ID the one used to send. It fails with ErrUnknownKey if the ring does not hold it.

### type MACAlgorithm

```go
type MACAlgorithm uint8
```

MACAlgorithm identifies the signature algorithm of an SPDU. The values are the code points of the IEC TR 61850-90-5 security algorithm table (carried on the wire in protocol version 1).

```go
const (
	MACNone          MACAlgorithm = 0
	MACHMACSHA256_80 MACAlgorithm = 1 // HMAC-SHA256 truncated to 80 bits
	// MACHMACSHA256_128 is HMAC-SHA256 truncated to 128 bits.
	MACHMACSHA256_128 MACAlgorithm = 2
	// MACHMACSHA256_256 is HMAC-SHA256, untruncated.
	MACHMACSHA256_256 MACAlgorithm = 3
	// MACAESGMAC64 (AES-GMAC, 64 bits) is not implemented.
	MACAESGMAC64 MACAlgorithm = 4
	// MACAESGMAC128 (AES-GMAC, 128 bits) is not implemented.
	MACAESGMAC128 MACAlgorithm = 5
)
```

MAC algorithms. Only the HMAC-SHA256 variants are implemented; an SPDU that uses another one is refused with ErrUnsupported.

```go
func (a MACAlgorithm) Size() int
```

Size returns the MAC length in octets, or 0 for MACNone and the algorithms this package does not implement.

### type SPDU

```go
type SPDU struct {
	// SI is the session identifier.
	SI SessionID

	// Number is the SPDU number, which a sender increments for every
	// SPDU.
	Number uint32

	// Version is the session protocol version, 1 or 2. Encode treats 0
	// as 2.
	Version uint16

	// TimeOfCurrentKey, TimeToNextKey and KeyID are the security
	// information. Encode takes them from the key and ignores these.
	TimeOfCurrentKey uint32
	TimeToNextKey    int16
	KeyID            uint32

	// Encryption and MAC are the algorithm octets of a version 1 SPDU
	// as decoded. Encode takes the MAC algorithm from the key.
	Encryption EncryptionAlgorithm
	MAC        MACAlgorithm

	// IV is the initialisation vector of a version 2 SPDU (empty unless
	// a peer encrypts). Encode sends it as given.
	IV []byte

	// Payloads are the APDUs carried.
	Payloads []Payload

	// Length is the SPDU length field as decoded. It is not checked:
	// implementations disagree on what it counts (docs/adr/0001).
	Length uint32

	// Signature is the signature value as decoded, nil when absent.
	Signature []byte

	// signed is the number of octets covered by the signature (the
	// offset of the signature tag); set by Decode.

}
```

SPDU is a session protocol data unit.

#### func Decode

```go
func Decode(b []byte) (*SPDU, error)
```

Decode strictly decodes the structure of an SPDU without verifying it (see [Verify](#func-verify)). Returned slices do not alias b.

It fails with a [\*DecodeError](#type-decodeerror) wrapping ErrMalformed for a datagram that is not a well-formed SPDU and ErrUnsupported for a protocol version other than 1 and 2.

### type Stats

```go
type Stats struct {
	Sent        uint64 // SPDUs sent
	SendErrors  uint64 // SPDUs that could not be sent
	Received    uint64 // frames delivered to Recv
	Dropped     uint64 // frames dropped because the queue was full
	Ignored     uint64 // valid SPDUs of another session identifier or payload type
	Malformed   uint64 // datagrams refused by the decoder or as unsupported
	Unsecured   uint64 // unsecured SPDUs refused
	UnknownKey  uint64 // SPDUs under a key the provider does not hold
	AuthFailed  uint64 // SPDUs whose signature did not verify
	Replayed    uint64 // SPDUs refused by the replay window
	OtherErrors uint64 // receive errors of the socket
}
```

Stats counts transport activity.

### type Transport

```go
type Transport struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Transport carries GOOSE or SV over UDP as R-GOOSE or R-SV. It implements [l2.Transport](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/l2#Transport) (goose.Transport, sv.Transport), so the goose and sv publishers and subscribers run over it unchanged: [Transport.Send](#func-transport-send) takes the layer-2 frame a publisher builds and sends its APDU in an SPDU; [Transport.Recv](#func-transport-recv) returns a layer-2 frame for each APDU of every SPDU that verifies.

A Transport is safe for concurrent use.

#### func Open

```go
func Open(cfg Config) (*Transport, error)
```

Open validates cfg, binds the socket, joins the multicast groups and starts receiving.

```go
func (t *Transport) Close() error
```

Close implements [l2.Transport](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/l2#Transport). Blocked Recv calls return ErrClosed; Close is idempotent.

#### func (Transport) Send

```go
func (t *Transport) Send(frame []byte) error
```

Send implements [l2.Transport](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/l2#Transport). frame is a layer-2 GOOSE or SV frame (optionally 802.1Q tagged) of the transport's kind; its APPID, simulation bit and APDU are sent in one SPDU to Config.RemoteAddr, secured with the provider's current key. The Ethernet addresses, VLAN tag and Reserved 2 are not carried.


Stats returns the transport counters.
